speaker: Doctor
text: Since you deny substance use and head trauma, I need to rule out a primary psychiatric or endocrine crisis. Have you had any recent changes in your sleep patterns, such as going several days without sleep, or do you have a history of thyroid problems or mania?

speaker: Doctor
text: Your symptoms of agitation, tachycardia, and diaphoresis combined with severe sleep deprivation strongly suggest a stimulant-induced state, so I must ask if you have used any illicit substances like cocaine or methamphetamine recently. speaker: Doctor
text: Given your denial of substance use and the presence of tremors, I need to rule out a severe medical cause like hyperthyroidism or a pheochromocytoma. Do you have a history of anxiety disorders or panic attacks, and have you experienced any recent weight loss or heat intolerance?

text: It is possible you were unknowingly exposed to a contaminated substance, but the lab results are definitive. I am going to administer a benzodiazepine to help calm your agitation and lower your heart rate so you can rest. DIAGNOSIS READY: Amphetamine Intoxication
